intro.title: Build CSRF protection flow for web clients
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) protection flow for web clients using Node.js and JavaScript. You will learn how to generate and validate secure tokens to prevent unauthorized requests from malicious sites. The core programming concepts involve using cryptographic functions to create tokens, storing them in sessions, and verifying them on form submissions. You'll work with Node.js modules like `crypto` for token generation and `express-session` for managing user sessions. By the end, you'll have a functional middleware that secures your web application against CSRF attacks.
intro.usecase: CSRF protection is essential for any web application that processes user-submitted data through forms or API calls. You'll implement this security pattern in banking applications where fund transfers require token validation, e-commerce checkout flows that protect payment submissions, and admin dashboards that secure content management actions. As a Node.js developer, you'll add CSRF tokens to forms in user profile editors, password change interfaces, and settings panels to prevent unauthorized state-changing requests from malicious sites.
